evidence_items.explanation: This 1998 study finds a generalization limitation for the tested parity-network architecture. It also finds improvements for addition and bit shifting, so its negative result is architecture- and task-specific.
The SCAN experiments show that recurrent networks successful on easier splits struggled to apply familiar components in systematically new combinations.

Apple's study documents reasoning fragility under controlled changes to arithmetic questions. Its results concern the tested models and tasks, rather than proving that all neural networks lack reasoning.

Lake and Baroni demonstrate human-like systematic generalization on their experimental tasks using specially trained neural networks. This is material counterevidence to an interpretation of permanent inability or no progress, but does not eliminate the later failures in e3.

unresolved_gaps: The selected studies establish recurring limitations, not a uniform annual measurement across all 26 years.
No single test covers every meaning of abstract reasoning or every neural-network architecture.
